title: Regional GPU Attrition & Replenishment Playbook — 24mo
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a 24-month attrition and replenishment plan for Redwood's GPU fleet across NA / EU / APAC. It focuses on the operational cadence for replacing decommissioned or failing hosts, planned retirement of older instance families, and the staggered replenishment footprint by cloud region to maintain latency SLAs and buffer targets. This is intentionally operational (runbook + numbers) rather than strategic procurement pricing.

Summary (one-liner):
Maintain a 12–18% rolling buffer across regions while replacing ~18% of fleet annually (mix H100/A100/L4) to keep performance and cost targets stable. Prioritize APAC first for replenishment windows in the next three quarters to reduce cross-region fallbacks.

Assumptions:
- Baseline fleet (2026-07-01): NA: 3,600 GPUs; EU: 2,400 GPUs; APAC: 1,200 GPUs (total 7,200).
- Attrition (hard failure + decommission) baseline: 0.6% per month region-agnostic ( ~7.2% annual), but effective attrition for planning uses 0.9% (includes early retirements, conversions).
- Planned lifecycle retirement: ~10% of fleet/year non-failure (older SKUs that no longer cost-effective). Combined effective annual churn target: 18% of fleet.
- Lead times: ordered capacity availability (cloud reservations / negotiated slots): H100: 8–12 weeks, A100: 6–10 weeks, L4: 4–8 weeks. Edge/on-prem ordering varies and is out-of-scope here.
- Buffer SLO: maintain >= 12% spare GPU capacity; critical trigger < 9%; emergency plan when < 6%.
- Target utilization bands (post-burst smoothing): steady-state 62–72% avg, peak 78–85% 95th percentile for short windows.

Planned replenishment mix (by quarter for next 24 months):
- Preference: H100 for latency-critical chat routes; A100 for balanced throughput jobs; L4 for embedding/cheap-low-latency workloads.
- Target mix at end of 24mo: H100 38%, A100 37%, L4 25% (by GPU count). Current mix (baseline): H100 25%, A100 50%, L4 25%.

Quarterly timeline snapshot (Q3 2026 -> Q2 2028):
- Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep): APAC focus. Replace 6% of APAC fleet with H100/A100 split 60/40. Reserve +1,200 L4-equivalent for embeddings later. Establish APAC warm pool.
- Q4 2026 (Oct-Dec): NA replenishment wave. Replace 7% overall NA fleet; create contingency reserve of 6% of NA fleet.
- Q1 2027 (Jan-Mar): EU targeted refresh for older A100 nodes; replenish 8% EU fleet (mix A100->H100 for 30% of replaced capacity).
- Q2 2027 (Apr-Jun): Cross-region balancing; move 4% ephemeral capacity (spot-like reserves) between NA/EU to handle seasonal demand.
- Q3 2027 (Jul-Sep): Capacity optimization pass (quantization + autoscaler tuning) to reduce effective capacity need by ~3–5% before next large PR.
- Q4 2027 (Oct-Dec): Final major replenishment to hit target mix; focus on firm reservations for H100 in NA and EU to lock latency-critical capacity for 2028.
- Q1 2028 (Jan-Mar): Stabilize, measure buffer compliance; adjust replacement cadence to observed attrition and utilization.
- Q2 2028 (Apr-Jun): Minor rebalancing to achieve region-level buffer parity.

Numeric forecast table (selected snapshots) — GPUs by region (count) and conservatively rounded:
- Baseline 2026-07-01: NA 3600, EU 2400, APAC 1200 = 7200 total.
- Target end Q4 2026 (2026-12-31): NA 3650, EU 2360, APAC 1265 = 7275 (small net growth + replenishment offsetting attrition).
- Target end Q4 2027 (2027-12-31): NA 3800, EU 2480, APAC 1500 = 7780 (growth + replacements to hit higher H100 mix).
- Target end Q2 2028 (2028-06-30): NA 3850, EU 2520, APAC 1525 = 7895 (final smoothing to target mix).

Attrition & replenishment mechanics (operational):
- Monthly review cadence: infra-capacity team runs an attrition reconciliation every 1st business day of the month comparing incident-driven retirements, scheduled retirements, and replacement orders.
- Replenishment policy: If effective available capacity (usable GPUs - reserved for canaries/QA) falls below Buffer SLO (12%), trigger fast-replace (prioritize L4/A100 replacement on non-latency routes, fast contract slots for H100 if needed).
- Rolling reorder band: place orders monthly for the upcoming 8–12 week window sized to cover predicted attrition + target growth / 12, with a monthly safety over-order of +1.5% to hedge lead-time variance.
- Hot-swap targets on failure: Reseat/redeploy within 4h for running jobs using fallback model variant; escalate to on-call infra if rebuild > 24h.

Region-specific notes and risks:
- APAC: higher hardware failure rate historically (slightly higher effective attrition). Priority for early replenishment to avoid cross-region fallbacks which increase p95 latency >15%. Risk: limited immediate H100 availability; contingency: short-term L4 burst zones and traffic shaping.
- EU: regulatory constraints increase lead-time for enterprise dedicated capacity (contracting artifacts). Plan to front-load reservations in Q1 2027.
- NA: largest fleet; most flexible in spot/commit mix. Maintain a 6% committed reserve and 6% warm on-demand buffer.

Runbook triggers (simple):
- Green: Buffer >= 14% and 7-day utilization stable; continue standard monthly ordering.
- Yellow: Buffer 9–13% or rising 95th pct utilization; increase reorder size by +3% and open procurement ticket for prioritized slots. Notify product SREs.
- Red: Buffer <= 8% or sustained 95th pct > 82% for 48h; execute emergency replenishment lane (activate reserved burst pools, reduce non-critical routes, accelerate H100 orders). Initiate postmortem if caused by unexpected mass failure.

Example short table (monthly cadence sample, July 2026 -> Sep 2026):
- 2026-07: NA available 3300 (util 68%), EU 2200 (util 66%), APAC 1000 (util 74%), buffer 13.3%
- 2026-08: failures (NA 8 GPUs, EU 5, APAC 12) -> monthly attrition ~0.35% observed. Procurement placed for replacement + growth.
- 2026-09: APAC replenishment completes +180 GPUs (mix 60% H100 / 40% A100), buffer increases to 14.1%.

Cost/back-of-envelope assumptions (for prioritization only):
- Unit monthly delta: H100 capacity slot cost ~ 3–4x A100; L4 ~ 0.45x A100. Use cost-to-performance comparisons per route before committing expensive H100 reserve.
- Budget note: prioritize H100 only where measured p95 latency regression >10% with A100; otherwise prefer A100 or L4.

Open questions & next steps (working list):
- Confirm vendor lead-time SLAs for additional H100 slots in APAC (owner: Aisha) — due 2026-07-23.
- Finalize 2027 replenishment PO schedule with finance for Q1-Q4 (owner: Marcus) — draft due 2026-08-05.
- Create a lightweight dashboard to show live buffer % by region and age-by-SKU (owner: Sasha) — spike due 2026-07-30.

Action items (immediate):
- [ ] Run attrition reconciliation for June 2026 and publish delta sheet (owner: Diego).
- [ ] Lock first APAC H100 tranche (owner: Aisha).
- [ ] Draft emergency reorder playbook for <6% buffer (owner: Marcus).
- [ ] Add an automated alert on Slack when region buffer drops below 11% (owner: SRE/Oncall).

Notes on document status:
- This is a working operational sheet. Numbers are conservative and intentionally include over-procurement buffer to handle lead time volatility. Revisions expected after vendor SLA confirmation and July procurement run.

Appendix (short glossary):
- Buffer = (idle available GPUs) / (total usable GPUs) measured at midnight UTC.
- Attrition = unscheduled + scheduled retirements measured as % of fleet per month.
- Warm pool = prewarmed nodes ready to serve within 2–6 minutes for burst windows.

End of sheet.
